Both pinned compiler profiles naturally link every target with zero remaining relocations. One ordinary inline scalar32 expression is reused for the two identical original bodies and all array elements; standard operation does not establish an upstream library identity.

Manual review corrected diagnostic-free pinned m2c drafts with typed pointer increments that skipped four elements for a four-byte original increment. No generated placeholders or assembly fallback are counted.

Wrapped 32-bit product/triple counts retain signed-positive gates and per-element forward alias propagation without signed C multiplication overflow. Raw float bit transfers introduce no numeric conversion.

Native 32-bit harness passed 146760 checks for exhaustive halfwords, raw integer special encodings, finite float bit conversions, fixed wrappers, untouched suffixes, shifted overlaps and wrapped signed count cases. Host float ABI tests do not prove EE special/FCR behavior.

Independent full-body review compared all 14 complete original instruction bodies with source/header/docs and found no defects in wrapped signed-positive products, raw transfers or forward pointer/store behavior. Registered metadata and targeted native harness are stable.
